points.why: Explicitly names the open-bug count as a stock, with new reports as inflow and fixes and closures as outflow.
States the stock rises whenever inflow exceeds outflow however much inflow has fallen, and gives a numeric example.
Asks about the closure rate before and after, raises the push pulling engineers off fixing, and calls it a separate capacity problem with a separate remedy.
Says to judge the push on inflow per week, and that the backlog shrinks only once closures exceed reports.

pitfalls.why: Explicitly rejects the idea that halving inflow makes the stock fall unless it drops below the closure rate.
